gap: None of the results ChatGPT got works out that refilling a BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 from a 12 V car socket takes about 20 hours of driving (1,910 Wh measured ÷ 96 W), or that BLUETTI's $1,099 Elite 200 V2 + Charger 1 bundle cuts this to about 3.4–4.8 hours and costs $100 less than the $1,199 Elite 200 V2 + 200 W panel kit.
standout_why: Powersized (powersized.com/best/rv/, cited) has the inputs but doesn't do the math. It gives the Elite 200 V2 car input as 96 W and the Charger 1 as 560 W at $299, which is stale (today it's $219). It only says a 4-hour drive adds 384 Wh, and it prices base stations with no kits. It never works out the full-refill driving time on either path, and it never compares the cost of the Charger 1 bundle with the panel kit. Eco Solar Kits (ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-rv-solar-kits, cited) gives only one driving figure, about 3 hours on Anker's 800 W alternator charger. It has no car-socket refill times and nothing for any BLUETTI or ALLPOWERS kit. I couldn't read Solargenadvisor (cited) because its TLS certificate was self-signed and the fetch was refused, so I can't rule out that it has this.
decides: The pick stays the Elite 200 V2, but the kit should change. For a van that drives most days, the $1,099 Elite 200 V2 + Charger 1 bundle refills in about 3.4–4.8 driving hours, against about 20 hours from the socket. That beats the $1,199 + 200 W panel kit, which needs about 10.4 hours of full rated sun. Add a panel later for parked days. The AC180 + Charger 1 at $748 does the same job for weekend vans, in about 2.1 hours because the AC180's 500 W input caps the charger. Our page's 'Charging while driving' column should list these bundles and the driving hours.

findings.note: 1,910 Wh ÷ 96 W = 19.9 h. Assumes the full rated 96 W. Charging losses not added.

findings.label: Max output, claim and price
findings.value: 560 W max; 'fully charge a 1kWh power station in just 2.5 hours'; $219 (list $249)

findings.note: BLUETTI's 2.5-hour claim works out to about 400 W average (1,000 Wh ÷ 2.5 h). BLUETTI says it works with all BLUETTI stations but publishes no model list. It connects to the car battery.

findings.label: Driving hours to refill with the alternator charger

findings.note: 1,910 Wh ÷ 560 W = 3.4 h. 1,910 Wh ÷ 400 W = 4.8 h. The Elite 200 V2's PV input (12–60 V, 20 A, 1,000 W) is well above 560 W, so it doesn't cap the charger.
